entries.name: Russian Twist
entries.reason: Own drawn frames on the seated chain (thigh 22.06, shin 22.47, spine 24.04 exact) with the trunk bearing 45 degrees back and the hands sweeping across the chest as the rotation read. Full notes and open questions in the daily review.
entries.summary: Five drawn positions of a Russian twist.

frames.caption: Sit tall with a long spine, the ribs stacked over the hips.
Turn the ribs one way - the arms just follow.
Hold the end of the turn under control.
Turn the ribs the other way on a slow count.
Return to centre with the spine long.

entries.name: Cross-Body Crunch
entries.reason: Redrawn on 8 October 2026 at the owner's request, because the earlier drawing contradicted this text: it showed straight legs and no knee coming in. Source-bound side-view draft with a spine that curls and shoulders that turn: knees bent, feet flat, hands by the head; the upper spine curls and turns so one shoulder and elbow lead across the body while the opposite knee comes in to meet them, a slower lowering, then the same to the other side. Seen from the side, the turn shows as one shoulder and elbow leading; the catalogue asks for a front view as well. The hands are drawn at the sides of the head: this figure cannot put a hand between the head and the floor.
entries.summary: Knees bent and feet flat, curl up and turn so one elbow and shoulder travel across while the opposite knee comes in to meet them, lower slowly, then repeat to the other side.

frames.caption: Lie on your back with the knees bent and the feet flat, hands resting lightly behind the head.
Curl up and turn so one elbow and shoulder travel across the body while the opposite knee comes in to meet them.
Lead with the shoulder. Curl the ribs toward the hips.
Then repeat to the other side.
The other shoulder leads and the other knee comes in to meet it.

entries.name: Oblique Crunches
entries.reason: Redrawn on 9 October 2026 at the owner's request, from the description accepted that day: the earlier drawing lifted a stiff trunk straight up, with no bench under the legs and no turn toward the opposite knee. Source-bound draft, drawn from a 3D model turned 12 degrees and seen from a little above, so the turn and the arm out on the floor show: lying on the floor with the lower legs on a bench, hips and knees at right angles, one hand beside the head and the other arm out on the floor; the upper spine curls and the shoulders turn, lifting the shoulder on the side of the raised hand and taking that elbow toward the opposite knee, a short pause, and a slower lowering. The legs and the hand on the floor do not move. One side is shown; the last caption carries the swap. The elbow is drawn short of touching the knee.
entries.summary: Lying with the lower legs on a bench, one hand beside your head and the other arm out on the floor, curl up and across to take that elbow toward the opposite knee, lower under control, then swap sides.

frames.caption: Lie on your back on the floor with the lower back pressed down and the lower legs resting on a bench so the hips and knees are bent to about ninety degrees, one hand beside your head and the other arm on the floor out to the side.
Keeping the legs still, lift the shoulder on the same side as the hand at your head and curl up and across, bringing that elbow toward the opposite knee.
Lower back stays down. Hand light on the head; do not pull.
Lower under control to the start.
Complete the repetitions, then swap arms and do the same on the other side.
